A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 25-page versions of the same work, with matching main sections, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–10, and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v2 reports original SpatialReasoner-R1 benchmark results and parameter ablations in Tables 1–4, plus qualitative successes and a failure case in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, parameter ablations, and qualitative results in Tables 1–4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The architecture, fDPO objective, spatial rewards, and M3CTS procedure remain unchanged. Replacing 'LLMs' with 'VLMs' aligns the prose with the multimodal models already specified in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OpenSpatial-derived training data and evaluate on SpatialRGPT-Bench and the same eight general vision-language benchmarks. The appendix examples cover the same scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all baseline models and SFT/DPO/fDPO variants; Table 2 retains the SpatialRGPT-8B comparison. Citation renumbering and model-name capitalization do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendices D–E retain the same training settings, model sizes, 657 qualitative and 749 quantitative evaluation pairs, GPT-4o judging, and ±25% quantitative success threshold. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The fDPO alpha and lambda sensitivity studies in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. Figure 4 and Appendix F retain the same qualitative comparisons and height-estimation failure analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Neither adds statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The abstract and introduction correct the reported average accuracy margin over the strongest baseline from 9.8% to 9.4%. Table 1's category margins are 2.90 and 15.88 percentage points, averaging 9.39. All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Around Equations (4)–(5), x/y notation is harmonized with the already defined T/R representation, and the preference dataset is written more compactly. Equation (10) renames the exploration coefficient from alpha to alpha-tilde. These are notation changes without altered mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The headline superiority claim is modestly narrowed from a 9.8% to a 9.4% average accuracy margin. The state-of-the-art claim and contributions involving interpretable LongCoT reasoning, fDPO, and M3CTS remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative examples are retained. Appendices G–H preserve the same impact discussion and limitations concerning explicit region inputs and extension beyond 2D spatial reasoning.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same reward instructions, evaluator identities, training hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and data-construction details. The project address is unchanged; prompt-title capitalization adds no technical information.

R1.justification: v3 consolidates the duplicate GPT-4o System Card references and updates Mulberry from its preprint citation to NeurIPS 2025. These identify the same underlying works; related-work coverage and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits standardize qualitative/quantitative terminology, LongCoT capitalization, and VLM wording, while harmonizing notation and cleaning bibliographic metadata. The section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 standardizes the SQA-TEST and 8B labels, and Figure 10 changes its title capitalization from LongCOT to LongCoT. Text, equations, and references reflow slightly; no figures or tables are added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the overstated headline margin from 9.8% to 9.4%, consistent with the simple average of Table 1's category margins, and reduces notation and terminology ambiguity. These provide limited improvements in reporting accuracy and clarity while leaving the method and empirical evidence unchanged.
